title: Parkour Runner with Undo/Redo
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a Three.js parkour runner game featuring undo/redo mechanics. Load the 3D model 'MosquitoInAmber.glb' using GLTFLoader from a CDN (use https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/ for Three.js and loaders).

SCENE SETUP:
- Create a perspective camera at position (0, 8, 15) looking toward the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (10, 20, 10) with intensity 1.0 and castShadow enabled.
- The ground is a series of floating platforms: generate 20 platforms as BoxGeometry(3, 0.5, 3) with MeshStandardMaterial in green (#44aa44). Place them in a path: platform[i] has x = i * 4 (spaced 4 units apart), y = Math.sin(i * 0.5) * 2 (varying heights between -2 and 2), z = Math.cos(i * 0.3) * 3 (slight zigzag). Store platforms in an array.
- Load 'MosquitoInAmber.glb' and scale it to (0.5, 0.5, 0.5). This is the player character (the 'runner'). Place it on top of platform[0] (centered on the platform, y adjusted so it sits on top).
- Add a skybox or background color of #87CEEB (sky blue).
- The camera should follow the runner smoothly: camera target position is (runner.x, runner.y + 8, runner.z + 15), lerp toward it each frame at factor 0.05.

PHYSICS / MOVEMENT:
- The runner has a velocity vector {x:0, y:0, z:0} and is affected by gravity: vy -= 25 * dt each frame.
- The runner's position updates each frame: pos += vel * dt.
- Ground collision: check if runner overlaps any platform (within platform bounds ±1.5 in x and z, and runner.y <= platform.y + 0.25 + runner's half-height ~0.5). If so, set runner.y to platform top, set vy = 0, set grounded = true. Track which platform index the runner is on (currentPlatform).
- If runner.y < -10, it's a fall. Auto-undo to last safe state.

USER INTERACTIONS:
- 'A' / 'D' or ArrowLeft / ArrowRight: move runner left/right (x-axis) at speed 6 units/sec.
- 'W' or ArrowUp: move runner forward (positive x direction) at speed 8 units/sec.
- 'S' or ArrowDown: move runner backward (negative x direction) at speed 4 units/sec.
- 'Space': jump if grounded. Set vy = 10. Set grounded = false.
- Each time the runner lands on a NEW platform (different currentPlatform than before), save a snapshot to the undo history stack. A snapshot stores: {position: {x,y,z}, velocity: {x,y,z}, currentPlatform, moveCount}.
- 'Z' key: UNDO - pop the last snapshot from undo stack, push current state to redo stack, teleport runner to that snapshot's position. Increment undoCount.
- 'Y' key: REDO - pop from redo stack, push current state to undo stack, teleport runner to that position. Increment redoCount.
- Any new move (landing on new platform) clears the redo stack.
- Track total moveCount (incremented each time runner lands on a new platform).

HUD / UI:
- Create a DOM overlay div at top-left showing: 'Platform: {currentPlatform}/19 | Moves: {moveCount} | Undos: {undoCount} | Redos: {redoCount}'.
- Add two HTML buttons: 'Undo (Z)' with id='undoBtn' and 'Redo (Y)' with id='redoBtn'. These should trigger the same logic as the Z/Y keys.
- Add a 'Reset' button with id='resetBtn' that resets the runner to platform 0 and clears all history.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
- runnerX, runnerY, runnerZ: runner's world position (numbers, 2 decimal precision is fine)
- velocityY: runner's vertical velocity
- grounded: boolean
- currentPlatform: integer index of current platform (0-19), or -1 if airborne/falling
- moveCount: integer total platform landings on new platforms
- undoCount: integer total undos performed
- redoCount: integer total redos performed
- undoStackSize: integer length of undo history
- redoStackSize: integer length of redo history
- platformCount: 20 (constant)
- modelLoaded: boolean, true once GLB is loaded
- fallen: boolean, true if runner fell below -10 (reset on undo)
- gameTime: elapsed time in seconds since start
physics_constraints: Gravity at 25 m/s², jump impulse vy=10, platform collision detection within ±1.5 units in x/z from platform center. Runner falls if y < -10. Undo/redo must perfectly restore position and velocity snapshots.
